paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima. (<ref>) An ensemble of k adapters leads to lower generalization errors and Hessian traces. Here, we fix the sum of the dimensions of k adapters to be equal to 256. (<ref>) QLoRA, which is trained on a quantized base model, yields lower generalization errors and Hessian trace values compared to LoRA.

model_annotations.English: The chart titled “Errors (COPA)” illustrates generalization error values for the COPA task across different adapter ranks, shown as paired bars per rank. The category axis is horizontal and labeled “Rank,” with four discrete categories ordered left to right as 4, 16, 64, and 256. The value axis is vertical (no explicit label shown) and uses a linear numeric scale with tick labels at approximately 0.0, 0.3, and 0.6, extending visually to a little above 0.7. For each rank, two adjacent bars are displayed—one blue and one green—each with black error bars and horizontal caps indicating variability/uncertainty. At rank 4, the blue bar is about 0.23 and the green bar about 0.20; at rank 16, the blue bar is about 0.24–0.25 and the green bar about 0.07–0.08; at rank 64, the blue bar is about 0.35 and the green bar about 0.16; and at rank 256, the blue bar is about 0.70 and the green bar about 0.67. The bars are grouped by rank (side-by-side within each group), no stacking is used, no legend is shown to define the colors, and there are no additional visual emphases beyond the error bars.
model_annotations.German: The chart titled “Errors (COPA)” illustrates empirical error values for the COPA task across different adapter ranks, shown as paired bars for each rank with uncertainty indicated by vertical error bars. The horizontal axis contains the categorical rank values labeled “Rank,” ordered from left to right as 4, 16, 64, and 256. The vertical axis is a numeric scale (linear) showing error magnitude with visible tick labels at approximately 0.0, 0.3, and 0.6, spanning from 0 up to roughly three-quarters of the plot (about 0.75). For each rank category, there are two adjacent bars: a blue bar on the left and a green bar on the right, each with black capped error bars. At rank 4, the blue bar is around 0.22 and the green bar is around 0.20; at rank 16, the blue bar is around 0.24 while the green bar is much shorter at about 0.07; at rank 64, the blue bar is around 0.35 and the green bar is around 0.16; and at rank 256, both bars are high, with the blue bar near 0.70 and the green bar near 0.67. The chart uses consistent grouping (two side-by-side bars per rank) without stacking, and there is no visible legend explaining the color mapping; no individual bars appear specially highlighted beyond the consistent color scheme and the presence of error bars on all bars.
